response: No, the timing of initial surfactant treatment does not make a significant difference in rates of chronic lung disease or mortality in premature infants, as long as it is administered early in the course of respiratory distress syndrome. Both early (less than 2 hours) and delayed (more than 2 hours) surfactant treatment have been shown to be effective in reducing the severity of respiratory distress syndrome, with no significant difference in long-term outcomes such as chronic lung disease or mortality. The most important factor is that surfactant is administered in a timely manner, rather than the exact timing of the initial dose.
